Set the angle of the view.
Set the scaling of the view.
If enabled, materials that animate over time will play in the viewport. If disabled, they hold their current frame.
How strongly vegetation moves in the viewport. The game's own wind varies by place, so this is an approximation of it.
The direction vegetation is blown in, in degrees.
Flags, cloth and creatures with baked vertex animations play them.
Hanging objects and leaves sway back and forth.
Flocks of birds flap and fly around their paths.
Materials blend their texture layers. If disabled, only the first layer is shown.
Materials apply their detail albedo and overlay normal textures.
Magma materials give off their flowing glow.
Materials give off light from their emissive textures.
Sky, clouds and flames are drawn unlit. This stands in for the game's shaders, which rely on its scene.
Water gets moving ripples and a smooth surface. This stands in for the game's shaders, which rely on its scene.
Fur is cut out into strands instead of being drawn as solid cards.
Light models inside environment boxes with the map's baked irradiance volumes, instead of the environment map. Outside every box, models keep the environment map's light.
The volumes' light is in the game's own units. Auto exposure scales it so the volumes' average matches the viewport's default ambient light. Current exposure: {0:F1}
Multiplies the volumes' light. With Auto Exposure off this is the exposure itself; around 25 matches typical maps.

The bake of the irradiance volumes to light the maps with, the NN of the map's envmap_NN files. Bakes are probably times of day; most Nightreign maps only have bake 0. A change applies the next time a map is loaded.

Blend the volumes' light towards a second bake, as the game does between times of day. The second bake's textures load with the map, so switching this on or changing the bake applies the next time a map is loaded.
The bake to blend towards. Volumes that don't have it keep the first bake's light.
How far towards the second bake: 0 is the first bake, 1 the second. Applies at once.

Scale the environment map's reflections by how bright the volumes' light is at each point compared with the volume's average, as the game does, so reflections darken in shadow and brighten in lit areas.

Take the sun's direction, color and intensity, the hemisphere ambient light, and the exposure from the map's GPARAMs, as the game does. The irradiance volumes then take the same exposure instead of their auto exposure, and the hemisphere replaces the grey environment map for ambient light and reflections. With several maps loaded, the first by name with its own GPARAM lights them all.

Multiplies the GPARAM's exposure. Most maps switch on the game's auto exposure, which adjusts the exposure to what is on screen; Smithbox uses the GPARAM's value as it is, so some maps may look too bright or too dark.

The GPARAM's hemisphere light (sky color from above, ground color from below) lights what the irradiance volumes don't cover, and the reflections. With this on it also adds to the volumes' light, which matches the game.
Light with {0}, the GPARAM the selected collision's scene GPARAM picks (its sub ID N picks mAA_BB_0N00), as the game does while the player is on it.
Select a collision whose scene GPARAM sub ID has a file in its area, to light with that GPARAM.
Light with the weather's version of the GPARAM: mAA_BB_CCWW, where WW is the weather's GparamId in WeatherParam. Areas without a file for the weather keep the plain one.
Time {0}: the GPARAMs' key for this timezone. In Elden Ring it is also the time irradiance volume bake {1} was made at.
Irradiance Volumes Follow the Time of Day

Light with the irradiance volume bakes of the time of day, blending between the two timezones either side of it, as the game does: bake N is timezone N. Every bake is loaded with the map, so the time can be changed without waiting; maps loaded before this was switched on load their other bakes as the time reaches them.
The bakes follow the time of day (Map Lighting): bake {0} towards {1} by {2:0.##}.
Light Characters with the Model Set

Light characters (c####) with the GPARAM LightSet's model set (ID {0}) instead of the scene's: its own sun, the fill lights (Light 1, which can turn with the camera, and the local lights) and its hemisphere. Not yet compared with the game, so it is off by default.
Fill the viewport's background with the BG color of the map's GPARAM (Setting Info), at the GPARAM's exposure, instead of the background color of the settings.
No loaded map has its own GPARAM, so the viewport's own sun is used.
The sun comes from the map's GPARAMs (the Map Lighting tab).
Light with the Lights Near the Camera
Light the viewports with the loaded maps' BTL lights near the camera, nearest first. When off, only selected lights shine. Selected lights always shine, wherever they are.
How far from the camera a light can be and still shine.
Also only light with a light within its own EnableDist of the camera, as the game turns it on. An EnableDist of 0 is taken as no limit.
The most lights shaded at once, the nearest kept. Every pixel checks each of them, so lower this if the viewport slows down.
Not used while the map's GPARAMs light the viewport: the lights' power is in the game's units, so it takes the GPARAM's exposure ({0:0.###}), as the sun does.
Lighting with {0} of the {1} lights in range.
Not used while the map's GPARAMs light the viewport: the volumes take the GPARAM's exposure, as the sun does.

The GPARAM each value is looked for in first. Values it doesn't have come from mapbase, then default.
Any of the project's GPARAMs can be chosen: one from another area lights every loaded map.
The time on the GPARAMs' TimeOfDay scale. Elden Ring keys its lighting at 0, 4, 8, 12, 15, 21 and 22.5, where 0 is morning, 12 evening and 15 night.
Volumes in the shading table: {0} of {1}
The linked environment boxes whose four textures of the bake are on the GPU. Boxes the game skips are left out.
{0}: {1} volumes in bake {2}, {3} of {4} environment boxes linked
Environment boxes without a volume: {0}, skipped by the game: {1}
Open the Irradiance Volumes tab of the Validation tools, which lists each environment box's volume and can fill their volume ID property from their names.
Set the gizmo to Translation mode.
Set the gizmo to Rotation mode.
Set the gizmo to Scale mode.
Place the gizmo origin based on the selection's local position.
Place the gizmo origin based on the selection's world position.
Orient the gizmo origin based on the world position.
Orient the gizmo origin based on the bounding box.
Whether to render objects in the viewport.
Whether to render textures in the viewport.
Whether to cull objects in the viewport outside of the camera frustum.
Whether models are lit by the baked irradiance volumes. When off, they take the ambient light outside the volumes instead. The same switch as the Global Illumination tab of the Rendering tool.

Whether the viewports are lit by the map's GPARAM lighting: its sun, hemisphere, exposure, tone map and background. When off, the Scene Lighting tab's own sun and settings are used. The same switch as the Map Lighting tab of the Rendering tool.
Whether the sun casts shadows. When off, the shadow maps aren't drawn. The same switch as the Shadows tab of the Rendering tool.
Whether to attempt to hide model masks based on entity NpcParam flags.
Determines the distance in front of the camera the placement orb is.
Determines the size of the compass.
Determines the angle offset when determining which direction is north.
Determines the radius of the dummy polygon mesh.
Determines the radius of the node mesh.
Determines the size of the dummy polygon ID and bone name text in the viewport.
Toggle which models are loaded during a map load.
Toggle which textures are loaded during a map load.

Holding click on the viewport will enable camera controls.
Use WASD to navigate.
Use right click to rotate the camera.
Hold Shift to temporarily speed up and Ctrl to temporarily slow down.
Scroll the mouse wheel to adjust overall speed.
Hold Ctrl, Alt and left click to make a box selection.

Holding click on the viewport will enable camera controls.
Pan the screen with the middle mouse button.
Use right click to rotate the camera.
Hold right click and scroll the mouse wheel to adjust the zoom.
Hold Ctrl, Alt and left click to make a box selection.

How the viewport's HDR scene is brought down to the screen. From GPARAM uses the map's Tone Map group under map lighting: ToneMapMode 8, which every Elden Ring GPARAM uses, is a Reinhard curve whose white point is the Reinhard Contrast times the Reinhard White Balance, and 7 is the filmic curve. This is an approximation of the game's curves, and anything without map lighting is clipped. Clamp clips at white, as the viewport did before it had an HDR target.
Multiplies the scene before the curve. The GPARAM's exposure is already applied to the map's lighting, so this is on top of it.
The brightness that the Reinhard curve takes to white, when the curve is set to Reinhard. From GPARAM uses the map's own.

Shadows cast by the sun, in up to four cascades. Under map lighting the cascade splits, the far fade and the bias come from the map's GPARAM Shadows group; otherwise from Elden Ring's mapbase. Only models drawn with the full material shader cast and receive them.
The size of each cascade's shadow map. The four cascades share one map twice this size on each side, for each viewport.
How much of the sun a shadow takes away: 1 for all of it.
Multiplies the GPARAM's Depth Bias and Slope Scaled Depth Bias. Raise it if surfaces shade themselves in stripes, lower it if shadows come away from what casts them.

Whether parts cast shadows as their IsShadowSrc or IsShadowOnly says, and receive them as their IsShadowDest says (ShadowSource and ShadowDest in DS3 and Bloodborne). Otherwise every part does both. Applies to parts as they are loaded or edited, so reload the map to apply it to all of them.
The map whose GPARAM lighting and irradiance bake light this editor's viewports, as it has no map of its own. Lit with: {0}. Shared by the Model and Time Act Editors.
The project has no map to borrow lighting from.
The irradiance volume of the map's bake to light with. Automatic takes the one whose average light is the median of the map's, among those with the most bakes.

The size of the box the volume is stretched over, centred on the origin. The volume's own box isn't read, so this isn't the game's scale; a smaller box shows more of the volume's variation across the model.
The map has no irradiance volumes.
